results.title: Sydney Morning Herald" Photo. Scene in the drawing-room at Admiralty House, Sydney, last week when the Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary in Australia of the United States of America, Mr. Clarence E. Gauss, presented his letters of credence to the Governor-General, Lord Gowrie. From the left, Mr. John Minter, First Secretary of the United States Legation, Lieut.-Colonel W. R. Hodgson, Mr. Gauss, Lord Gowrie, Mr. R. G. Menzies, Prime Minister, and Mr. McEwen. The 6000-ton French passenger liner Meknes, which, while on her way from England to France carrying 1300 Frenchmen who had elected to return home and take no further part in the war, was sunk on Wednesday night by a German motor torpedo-boat, which fired on her without warning. Passengers and crew were given five minutes to take to the boats, and the ship was then torpedoed, sinking in less . than five Minutes with the loss of some three hundred lives. (Evening Post, 27 July 1940)
